---
title: Authentication
description: Secure your API requests with Pinnacle API keys
---

## Overview

The Pinnacle API authenticates requests using API keys that you can generate and manage in your [Pinnacle Dashboard](https://app.pinnacle.sh/dashboard/development/api-keys). Every API request must include a valid API key to access Pinnacle's services.

## Using Your API Key

Pinnacle uses the `PINNACLE-API-KEY` header for authentication. Include your API key in every request:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.pinnacle.sh/status" \
  -H "PINNACLE-API-KEY: your_api_key_here"
```

## Authentication Errors

If your API key is missing, invalid, or expired, Pinnacle will return a `401 Unauthorized` response:

```json
{
  "error": "Invalid API key."
}
```

---
title: Purchase Phone Numbers
description: Search for and purchase phone numbers for your messaging campaigns.
---

Phone numbers are required for sending SMS and MMS messages through 10DLC and toll-free campaigns.

## Search available numbers

Find numbers that match your requirements with [`POST /phone-numbers/search`](/api-reference/phone-numbers/search).

### Filters

- **Location**: Find numbers in specific regions
- **Digits**: Match specific digits in the number
- **Features**: Filter by features such as SMS, MMS, voice, etc.
- **Number type**: Choose between local and toll-free

## Purchase numbers

Once you've found suitable numbers, buy them through [`POST /phone-numbers/buy`](/api-reference/phone-numbers/buy).

- **Processing time**: Immediate
- **Status check**: [`GET /status/phone-number/{phoneNumber}`](/api-reference/status/phone-number)

## Best practices

- Purchase multiple numbers for high-volume campaigns to distribute load
- Keep spare numbers ready for quick scaling
- Monitor number health and reputation regularly
- Rotate numbers periodically for long-running campaigns

## Next steps

After purchasing numbers, you need to attach them to your campaign before you can send messages.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="10DLC">
    Local 10-digit numbers for A2P messaging.

    See [10DLC campaigns](/guides/campaigns/10dlc#attach-number-to-campaign) to send your first message.

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Toll-Free">
    Numbers starting with 800, 833, 844, 855, 866, 877, or 888.

    See [toll-free campaigns](/guides/campaigns/toll-free#attach-number-to-campaign) to send your first message.

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="RCS">
    Rich Communication Services for enhanced messaging. Phone numbers are not required for RCS campaigns but can be used for SMS fallback.

    See [RCS campaigns](/guides/campaigns/rcs) for setup instructions.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

---
title: Register Your Brand
description: >-
  Step-by-step guide for creating, submitting, and monitoring a brand with The
  Campaign Registry via Pinnacle.
---

Carriers check your brand before they approve any campaign. Register it once and reuse the resulting `brandId` across 10DLC, Toll-Free, and RCS flows.

⏱️ **Approval time:** Less than 15 minutes

## Prerequisites

- Legal entity name (and DBA if applicable) plus a website that matches public records
- Federal EIN or Tax ID, business address, and a reachable support contact
- Vertical, use case, and opt-in details that carriers can audit later

## Step 1: Create or update the brand

- Upsert the record with [`POST /brands`](/api-reference/brands/upsert). Re-send the request with specific fields whenever you need to fix data before submission.
- Call the optional helpers:

<Callout type="tip" title="Optional helpers">
  - [`POST /brands/autofill`](/api-reference/brands/autofill) uses the brand name, website, and/or additional info to fill in the brand information.
  
  
  - [`POST /brands/validate`](/api-reference/brands/validate) checks for common
  formatting and brand issues. Treat the response as advisory feedback — we surface major
  concerns but never block submission.

</Callout>

## Step 2: Submit for verification

- Push the profile for review with [`POST /brands/{brandId}/submit`](/api-reference/brands/submit).
- Request additional vetting for higher throughput with [`POST /brands/{brandId}/vet`](/api-reference/brands/vet).
- Standard verification completes in under 15 minutes; optional vetting typically finishes within one to three business days.

## Step 3: Monitor and refresh status

- Retrieve the full record with [`GET /brands/{id}`](/api-reference/brands/get) whenever you need the latest carrier response.
- Force a status refresh through [`GET /status/brand/{brandId}`](/api-reference/status/brand).

---
title: Campaigns Overview
description: Choose the right messaging campaign type for your use case.
---

Campaigns are required for compliant messaging across different channels. Each campaign type has specific requirements and approval processes.

## Campaign types

<Cards cols={3}>
  <Card title="10DLC" icon="fa-solid fa-mobile" href="/guides/campaigns/10dlc">
    Local 10-digit A2P messaging for high-volume SMS/MMS campaigns in the US.
  </Card>
  <Card
    title="Toll-Free"
    icon="fa-solid fa-phone"
    href="/guides/campaigns/toll-free"
  >
    Toll-free messaging for nationwide reach with higher throughput limits.
  </Card>
  <Card title="RCS" icon="fa-solid fa-comments" href="/guides/campaigns/rcs">
    Rich Communication Services for interactive messaging with cards and
    carousels.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## Quick comparison

| Feature                              | 10DLC      | Toll-Free     | RCS                            |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------- | ------------- | ------------------------------ |
| **Approval time**                    | 1-2 days   | < 10 mins[^1] | 2-4 weeks                      |
| **Throughput (msg segments/minute)** | 75-225[^2] | 1000          | Unlimited                      |
| **Media support**                    | SMS/MMS    | SMS/MMS       | Rich cards, carousels, buttons |
| **Geographic reach**                 | US only    | US only       | Global                         |
| **Number required**                  | Yes        | Yes           | No (agent-based)               |

## Prerequisites

Before creating any campaign, you'll need:

1. **Registered brand** - [Create your brand](/guides/brands) first
2. **Compliance documentation** - Opt-in flows, sample messages, terms of service
3. **Use case details** - Clear description of your messaging purpose

## Getting started

<Steps>
  <Step title="Register your brand">
    All campaigns require a verified brand. [Start here →](/guides/brands)
  </Step>
  <Step title="Choose campaign type">
    <Tabs>
      <Tab title="10DLC">
        **Choose this if you need:** Medium volume, local presence

        - Approval time: 1-2 days
        - Throughput: 75-225 msg/min
        - Local 10-digit numbers
        - Ideal for businesses targeting specific regions

        [Get started with 10DLC →](/guides/campaigns/10dlc)
      </Tab>
      <Tab title="Toll-Free">
        **Choose this if you need:** High volume, nationwide reach

        - Approval time: < 10 minutes. 2-3 days for carrier review of numbers.
        - Throughput: 1000 msg/min
        - Recognizable toll-free numbers

        [Get started with Toll-Free →](/guides/campaigns/toll-free)
      </Tab>
      <Tab title="RCS">
        **Choose this if you need:** Rich media, interactive features

        - Approval time: 2-4 weeks
        - Unlimited throughput
        - Cards, carousels, and buttons
        - No phone number required

        [Get started with RCS →](/guides/campaigns/rcs)
      </Tab>
    </Tabs>

  </Step>
  <Step title="Submit for approval">
    Follow the specific guide for your chosen campaign type
  </Step>
  <Step title="Attach numbers & send">
    Purchase numbers (if needed) and start messaging
  </Step>
</Steps>

[^1]: Toll-free campaigns are reviewed in less than 10 minutes. However, the numbers are reviewed by carriers one by one and may take 2-3 days to go live.

[^2]: Throughput varies based on brand type, brand's trust score, and campaign use case.

---
title: 10DLC Campaigns
description: 'Register, submit, and launch compliant 10DLC messaging campaigns.'
---

Follow the sequence below to start sending production 10DLC traffic.

⏱️ **Approval time:** Around 1-2 days

## Prerequisites

- A verified `brandId` ([register one here](/guides/brands))
- Documented opt-in, help, and opt-out copy that matches your actual flows
- Sample outbound messages covering the content you intend to send

## Step 1: Create or update the campaign

- Call [`POST /campaigns/dlc`](/api-reference/campaigns/10-dlc/upsert) with the brand, use case, keywords, sample messages, and compliance metadata.

<Callout type="tip" title="Optional helpers">
  - [`POST /campaigns/dlc/autofill`](/api-reference/campaigns/10-dlc/autofill) fills in the campaign information based on the existing information for a campaign and its brand.
  
  - [`POST /campaigns/dlc/validate`](/api-reference/campaigns/10-dlc/validate) surfaces
  formatting and campaign issues. Treat the response as guidance only; it never
  blocks campaign submission but is intended to guide you.

</Callout>

## Step 2: Submit for carrier review

- Call [`POST /campaigns/dlc/submit/{campaignId}`](/api-reference/campaigns/10-dlc/submit) to submit the campaign for carrier review.
- Changes may be requested and you will need to resubmit.

## Step 3: Watch review progress

- Pull the full record and its status with [`GET /campaigns/dlc/{campaignId}`](/api-reference/campaigns/10-dlc/get).
- Force a status refresh using [`GET /status/dlc-campaign/{campaignId}`](/api-reference/status/dlc-campaign).

## Step 4: Attach numbers and start sending messages

### Purchase phone numbers

See our [phone numbers guide](/guides/phone-numbers) for detailed instructions on searching and purchasing numbers.

### Attach number to campaign

Attach owned numbers to the campaign via [`POST /phone-numbers/attach-campaign`](/api-reference/phone-numbers/attach-campaign).

- Processing time: Up to 10 minutes
- Status check: [`GET /status/dlc-campaign/{campaignId}`](/api-reference/status/dlc-campaign)

### Send messages

Start messaging with [`POST /messages/send/sms`](/api-reference/messages/send-sms) or [`POST /messages/send/mms`](/api-reference/messages/send-mms). While waiting for approval, you'll also be able to send test messages with our sandbox numbers. See our [sending messages guide](/guides/messages/sending#sending-from-a-number) for detailed instructions on sending messages.

---
title: Messaging Overview
description: 'Orchestrate SMS, MMS, and RCS conversations with a single API.'
---

Connect with customers on their preferred channels while managing every aspect of your messaging lifecycle through Pinnacle. Begin with our sending guide to get started quickly, then expand your capabilities with advanced message status tracking and inbound message handling as your needs grow.

<Cards cols={2}>
  <Card
    title="Send messages"
    icon="fa-solid fa-paper-plane"
    href="/guides/messages/sending"
  >
    Build SMS, MMS, and RCS experiences with step-by-step API examples and
    channel-specific tips.
  </Card>
  <Card
    title="Receive replies"
    icon="fa-solid fa-inbox"
    href="/guides/messages/receiving"
  >
    Listen for webhooks, track message statuses, and turn responses into
    meaningful conversations.
  </Card>
</Cards>

## Channels at a glance

| Channel | Best for                             | Sender                    | Highlights                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **SMS** | Alerts, 2FA, concise notifications   | 10DLC or toll-free number | Instant reach, text only                                                                                                                                                              |
| **MMS** | Rich promotions, media-heavy updates | 10DLC or toll-free number | [Images, GIFs, PDFs](https://app.pinnacle.sh/supported-file-types?type=MMS) alongside text                                                                                            |
| **RCS** | Interactive journeys, commerce flows | Approved RCS agent        | [Cards](https://app.pinnacle.sh/supported-file-types?type=RCS-CARD), [rich media](https://app.pinnacle.sh/supported-file-types?type=RCS-MEDIA), buttons, quick replies, read receipts |

## Before you send

- **Numbers or agent credentials.** Purchase a number or get an agent ID by registering an [RCS campaign](/guides/campaigns/rcs).
- **Campaign approval.** Ensure each number is attached to an active 10DLC/toll-free campaign, or your RCS agent is approved.
- **API access.** Create an API key on the [Pinnacle Dashboard](https://app.pinnacle.sh/dashboard/development/api-keys) and store it securely.

<Callout type="tip" title="Optional: Validate first">
  Use [`POST /messages/validate/sms`](/api-reference/messages/validate-sms),
  [`POST /messages/validate/mms`](/api-reference/messages/validate-mms), and
  [`POST /messages/validate/rcs`](/api-reference/messages/validate-rcs) to allow
  you to validate content without sending. This will help you catch unsupported
  files, return media size, display segmentation, and give cost estimates before
  hitting send.
</Callout>

## Send in three steps

<Steps>
  <Step title="Compose">Craft the SMS, MMS, or RCS message to be sent.</Step>
  <Step title="Deliver">
    Use the respective send endpoint/method.

    - SMS: [`POST /messages/send/sms`](/api-reference/messages/send-sms).
    - MMS: [`POST /messages/send/mms`](/api-reference/messages/send-mms).
    - RCS: [`POST /messages/send/rcs`](/api-reference/messages/send-rcs).

  </Step>
  <Step title="Track">
    Poll [`GET /messages/{messageId}`](/api-reference/messages/get) to get
    updates for your message or subscribe to webhooks to monitor status changes
    and inbound replies. See our [receiving guide](/guides/messages/receiving)
    for more details.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Next up

- Keeping track of conversations? Explore [Conversations API](/api-reference/conversations).
- Ready to receive messages and message statuses? Continue to [Receiving messages](/guides/messages/receiving).

---
title: Sending Messages
description: 'Deliver SMS, MMS, and RCS experiences with Pinnacle''s Messaging API.'
---

Choose your sending method based on your channel and use case.

<Cards cols={2}>
  <Card
    title="SMS and MMS"
    icon="fa-solid fa-phone"
    href="#sending-from-a-number"
  >
    Use 10DLC or toll-free numbers for traditional SMS and MMS messaging with
    broad reach and reliable delivery.
  </Card>
  <Card title="RCS" icon="fa-solid fa-robot" href="#sending-from-an-rcs-agent">
    Deploy rich, interactive messaging experiences through approved RCS agents
    with cards, buttons, and media.
  </Card>
</Cards>

---

## Sending from a number

SMS and MMS messages are sent from a 10DLC or toll-free number that is linked to an approved campaign.

### Prerequisites

0. API key from the [Pinnacle Dashboard](https://app.pinnacle.sh/dashboard/development/api-keys).
1. Purchased 10DLC or toll-free number. See our [phone numbers guide](/guides/phone-numbers) for detailed instructions on searching and purchasing numbers.
2. Verified brand ([register one here](/guides/brands))
3. Attach number to campaign.
   - For 10DLC, see our [10DLC guide](/guides/campaigns/10dlc#attach-number-to-campaign).
   - For toll-free, see our [toll-free guide](/guides/campaigns/toll-free#attach-number-to-campaign).

### Workflow

<Steps>
  <Step title="Craft the message">
    Create your message with text for SMS or text and media for MMS.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Provide sender & recipient">
    Include `from` and `to` in E.164 format (for example `+14155550123`).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Configure options">
    Customize delivery with scheduling, tracking, and validation options.
    - **Scheduling**: Schedule messages for future delivery and at a specified cadence.
    - **Tracking**: Ensures precision when reacting to messages. If disabled, reactions still work but may react to a different message. This adds an ID to the end of the message that can be `HIDDEN`.
    - **Validation**: Validate content before sending. This catches errors without consuming credits. See our validation endpoints for [SMS](/api-reference/messages/validate-sms) and [MMS](/api-reference/messages/validate-mms).
    - **Multiple messages (MMS only)**: Large MMS payloads across multiple messages when media exceeds carrier limits. SMS messages are always split into multiple messages.

  </Step>
  <Step title="Send the message">
    Call [`POST /messages/send/sms`](/api-reference/messages/send-sms) for SMS or [`POST /messages/send/mms`](/api-reference/messages/send-mms) for MMS.
  </Step>
</Steps>
### Media support

Check supported file types and size limits for MMS messages at [app.pinnacle.sh/supported-file-types?type=MMS](https://app.pinnacle.sh/supported-file-types?type=MMS).

### Sandbox numbers

While waiting for approval, you can still craft flows and send messages to your own phone number. Request a sandbox number through the [Sandbox Numbers section](https://app.pinnacle.sh/dashboard/development/sandbox-numbers). These numbers require no campaign approval and are perfect for integration testing before production. Note that you must whitelist the recipient phone number on the same page before you can send messages to it.

### Best practices

- Always use E.164 format for phone numbers.
- Monitor webhook events for delivery status.
- Respect segment limits - long SMS messages are split and billed per segment.
- Verify numbers are attached to approved campaigns.

---

## Sending from an RCS agent

RCS unlocks branded, interactive conversations with cards, buttons, and rich media. Each message must be sent from an approved agent ID (`agent_XXXXXXXXXXXX`) linked to your RCS campaign.

### Prerequisites

0. You'll need an API key from the [Pinnacle Dashboard](https://app.pinnacle.sh/dashboard/development/api-keys).
1. You'll need to have a verified brand ([register one here](/guides/brands))
2. You'll need an approved RCS agent ID from a registered [RCS campaign](/guides/campaigns/rcs).

### Workflow

<Steps>
  <Step title="Craft the message">
    Create your message with text, media, or carousel-style cards. Add quick
    replies or buttons to enhance user interactions.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Provide sender & recipient">
    Include `from` with your agent ID (e.g., `agent_XXXXXXXXXXXX`) and `to` in
    E.164 format.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Configure options">
    Customize with test mode, validation, tracking, and scheduling options.

    - **Test mode**: Send from Pinnacle's test agent without campaign approval
    - **Validation**: Check content without sending to catch errors early. See our validation endpoints for [RCS](/api-reference/messages/validate-rcs).
    - **Tracking**: Ensures precision when reacting to messages. If disabled, reactions still work but may react to a different message. This adds an ID to the end of the message that can be `HIDDEN`. This only works for RCS text messages.
    - **Scheduling**: Schedule messages for future delivery at specified times

  </Step>
  <Step title="Send the message">
    Call [`POST /messages/send/rcs`](/api-reference/messages/send-rcs) to
    deliver your RCS message.
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Content types

**Text messages**: Simple text with optional quick replies for user interactions. Can fit a lot more text (3000 characters) than SMS (160 characters).

**Media messages**: Single image or video with text overlay and action buttons. Can fit a lot more media (100MB) than MMS (1MB).

**Card carousels**: Swipeable cards with individual media, titles, subtitles, and buttons. Perfect for product showcases or multi-option selections.

**Quick replies**: Chip suggestions that appear below the message. There are several types of quick replies that encode different actions.

**Buttons**: Similar to quick replies, but appear on the message itself.

For more details check out our [API reference](/api-reference/messages/send-rcs).

### Media support

Check supported formats and limits for [media files](https://app.pinnacle.sh/supported-file-types?type=RCS-MEDIA) and [card images](https://app.pinnacle.sh/supported-file-types?type=RCS-CARD).

### Test agents

While waiting for approval of your production RCS agent, you will be granted access to a test agent. You can use this to test full RCS functionality. Note that you must whitelist the recipient phone number on your RCS campaign page before you can send messages to it. Make sure to use the `options.test_mode` flag to send from the test agent.

There are two types of test agents:

- Pinnacle's test agent (with Pinnacle's branding)
- Brand's specific test agent (with the brand's logo, icons, etc.)

At first you will be granted access to Pinnacle's test agent. When available, you will be granted access to the brand's specific test agent. This switch happens automatically but you'll need to whitelist the recipient phone numbers again for the brand's test agent.

### Best practices

- Always prefix agent IDs with `agent_`.
- Test media assets with validation endpoint before production.
- Monitor delivery and read receipts via webhooks.

- Pinnacle's test agent (with Pinnacle's branding)
- Brand's specific test agent (with the brand's logo, icons, etc.)

- Always prefix agent IDs with `agent_`.
- Test media assets with validation endpoint before production.
- Monitor delivery and read receipts via webhooks.

---
title: Receive inbound messages
subtitle: Receive inbound messages from Pinnacle.
---

## Add a Webhook

You can add testing webhooks on the [testing page](https://dashboard.trypinnacle.app/settings/testing). For other webhooks, you can configure them on the [webhooks page](https://dashboard.trypinnacle.app/webhooks). Once you add your webhook, you will be provided with a `PINNACLE-SIGNING-SECRET` that will be sent alongside all inbound requests. Keep this secret safe, as it will be used to authenticate requests.

## Receiving Inbound Messages

All inbound messages (SMS, MMS, and RCS) will be sent as a POST request to your webhook URL. Inbound messages can be categorized into four types:

- Inbound Text Messages: Standard text messages sent by users.
- Inbound Media Messages: Messages that contain media (images, audio, video, files).
- Inbound Action Messages (RCS only): Messages when the user interacts with buttons or quick replies.
- Inbound Location Messages (RCS only): Messages that contain location coordinates in latitude and longitude.

Each message will contain a few common fields, as well as specific fields depending on the message type. The common fields are:

```json
{
  "from": "Sender's phone number or brand name (i.e. +1234567890 or [[TEST]] Pinnacle Software Development Inc.)",
  "to": "Recipient's phone number (i.e. +1234567890)",
  "messageType": "Type of message. One of 'text', 'media', 'action', or 'location'",

  // Message-type specific fields

  "metadata": {
    "sender": {
      "city": "City or comma-separated cities of the sender",
      "state": "State or region of the sender",
      "country": "Country of the sender"
    },
    "message": {
      "timestamp": "Timestamp of when the message was sent in ISO 8601 format (i.e. 2022-01-01T12:00:00Z)"
    }
  }
}
```

### Inbound Text Messages

Occurs when the user sends a text message. It will contain the following additional text field:

```json
{
  "messageType": "text",
  "text": "Text of the message"
}
```

### Inbound Media Messages

Occurs when the user sends a media message (i.e. files and/or images sent). It will contain the following additional fields:

```json
{
    "messageType": "media",
    "text": "Text in the message if any",
    "mediaUrls": [
        {
            "type": : "MIME type of the media (i.e. image/jpeg).",
            "url": "URL of media"
        },
        ...
    ]
}
```

#### Note for RCS Media Messages

- If multiple images and text are sent in a single message, they will be received as separate text and media messages.
- The `mediaUrls.type` field will always be `file`. MIME types for RCS media messages is coming soon.

### Inbound Action Messages (RCS only)

Occurs when the user interacts with buttons or quick replies. It will contain the following additional fields:

```json
{
  "messageType": "action",
  "actionTitle": "Title of the action button clicked",
  "payload": "Payload associated with the action. Only for 'trigger' actions.",
  "actionMetadata": "Additional metadata associated with the action. Only for 'trigger' actions."
}
```

Note that for `trigger` actions, you'll have access to the `payload` and `actionMetadata` fields.

For any other action types, only the `actionTitle` will be available (in addition to the `messageType`). This means that that action was tapped on.

### Inbound Location Messages (RCS only)

Occurs when the user sends a location to the bot. It will contain the following additional location fields:

```json
{
  "messageType": "location",
  "coordinates": {
    "lat": "Latitude of the location",
    "lng": "Longitude of the location"
  }
}
```

## Authenticating Requests

To authenticate inbound requests, you will need to add a webhook to your account. This will give you a `PINNACLE-SIGNING-SECRET` that will be sent alongside all inbound requests. For example:

```
PINNACLE-SIGNING-SECRET: <your-signing-secret>
```

You will need to verify this secret in your application to ensure that the request is coming from Pinnacle. Note that headers are [case-insensitive](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-field-names) so they may have different casing depending on the language and framework you are using.

## Language-native type definitions

### Python

To type inbound messages, use the `Pinnacle.parse_inbound_message(message: dict)` static method. This method will return the appropriate inbound message type based on the message type.

```python
from rcs import Pinnacle

Pinnacle.parse_inbound_message(json_data)
```

### Typescript

To type inbound messages, use the `Pinnacle` namespace. For example:

```typescript
import { Pinnacle } from "rcs-js";

// Available types:
// - InboundMessage
// - InboundTextMessage
// - InboundMediaMessage
// - InboundActionMessage
// - InboundLocationMessage
requestBody as Pinnacle.InboundActionMessage;
```

### Ruby

To type inbound messages, use the `Pinnacle::{{INBOUND_MESSAGE_TYPE}}.from_json(json_object: json_body)` method where `json_body` is a JSON string. For example:

```ruby
# Available types (INBOUND_MESSAGE_TYPE):
# - InboundMessage
# - InboundActionMessage
# - InboundLocationMessage
# - InboundMediaMessage
# - InboundTextMessage

Pinnacle::InboundTextMessage.from_json(json_object: json_body)
```

## Examples

See our [hackathon projects](https://github.com/pinnacle-dev/hackathons) for examples of how to handle inbound messages. If you have any questions, feel free to reach out to our support team. Happy coding! 🎉

title: Receive message statuses
subtitle: Listen for message status changes.
---

## Provide a status callback URL

When sending a message with the Pinnacle SDKs, you can provide an optional `statusCallback` URL. This URL will be called with the status of the message changes. See the [send docs](api-reference/send-a-message) for more information.

## Receive message statuses

When the status of a message changes, Pinnacle will send a POST request to the `statusCallback` URL you provided. The request will contain a JSON payload with the following fields:

- `messageId`: The ID of the message.
- `status`: The new status of the message. Possible values are:
  - `pending`: The message is pending.
  - `sent`: The message has been sent.
  - `send_failed`: The message failed to send.
  - `delivered`: The message has been delivered.
  - `delivery_failed`: The message failed to deliver.
  - `received`: The message has been received by the recipient.
  - `read`: The message has been read by the recipient. This status is only available for RCS messages.

Here is an example of the JSON payload:

```json
{
  "messageId": "123456",
  "status": "sent"
}
```

endpoints.description:
Whitelist a phone number for testing with your test RCS agent.

## Overview
During development and testing, RCS agents can only send messages to whitelisted phone numbers.
Use this endpoint to add test devices to your agent's whitelist before sending test messages.

## Verification Process
After whitelisting a number, you'll need to complete verification:

1. Check the test device for an "RBM Tester Management" request
2. Accept the request on the device
3. Enter the 4-digit verification code in the Pinnacle dashboard at:
   ```
   https://app.pinnacle.sh/dashboard/brands/{brandId}?campaignId={campaignId}&campaignType=RCS
   ```

> **Important Notes**
>
> - **Testing only:** This is only required for test agents. Production agents can message any RCS-enabled number
> - **AT&T limitation:** Whitelisting may currently fail for AT&T numbers
> - **Verification required:** The whitelist request isn't complete until you verify the device.
